title: Add perf-canary gate for kernel selector v2 (thresholds + dashboard links)
author: Sahana Iyer
description: Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 (selector v2) changes kernel choice based on model family + seq-length regime (prefill/decode buckets) + GPU SKU. We need a CI perf-canary gate that (a) runs a representative benchmark matrix and (b) fails if v2 regresses beyond agreed budgets, with direct links to dashboards/artifacts for triage. This PR adds a new perf-canary gate definition for selector v2, wires it into our CI entrypoints, and standardizes artifact/dash links (Grafana + trace explorer + results table). Gate scope: hosted-style mixed prompt distributions (short/medium/long), evaluated across L4/A10/A100/H100 for the top families (Llama-family, Mistral-family, Qwen-family) and both prefill-heavy and decode-heavy regimes. Thresholds are aligned with SRE rollout guardrails and are intended to catch the A10 long-context tail regression class we saw in earlier canaries while still allowing small measurement noise. What’s included: (1) New gate config: selector_v2_perf.yaml with explicit thresholds and per-SKU overrides; (2) Results schema: adds selector_version and seq_bucket grouping to output summary for easier diffing; (3) CI integration: updates GitHub Actions workflow to run gate on demand (workflow_dispatch) and on the nightly canary schedule, and documents how runtime PRs can invoke it via the existing /perf-canary slash command; (4) Dashboard links: adds canonical links into the job summary to the selector v2 dashboards (kernel choice heatmap, selector version breakdown, p95 latency by GPU + seq bucket) and to the artifact bundle. Thresholds (high level): - P95 end-to-end latency regression budget: <= +5% overall vs baseline (selector v1) for each {model_family, gpu_sku}; for long-context bucket (effective_context >= 8k) allow <= +8% on L4 only (known measurement variance), but keep <= +5% on A10/A100/H100. - Throughput (tok/s) regression: >= -3% overall; >= -5% allowed for long-context on H100 only when prefill dominates (batching variance). - P50 latency regression: <= +3%. - Error rate / correctness proxy: run must have 0 crashes; server-side errors <= 0.1% (primarily to catch misconfig / incompatible kernel selection failures in the harness). - Min sample size: require >= 200 requests per bucket before enforcing strict thresholds; below that, gate reports “insufficient sample” and marks as non-blocking but still posts dashboards. Notes: Gate compares v2 vs v1 within the same run where possible (paired runs), falling back to last green baseline artifact for that GPU if capacity prevents paired. Gate is deterministic in bucketing (same bucket boundaries as runtime selector v2 docs) to reduce false deltas. This does NOT change runtime code; it only updates perf-canary. Rollout: We’ll keep the gate non-blocking for 1 week (nightly only) to establish baseline variance and then flip it to blocking for selector v2 rollout stages (tracked in ENG-3930).

conversation: Marcus Reed (review): The thresholds look reasonable, but can you call out explicitly which metric we’re diffing for tok/s (mean vs median) and whether it’s normalized by concurrency? We’ve had confusion before when concurrency changes between paired runs.

Sahana Iyer (author): Good catch. Right now we diff mean tok/s at fixed concurrency=16 (pinned in the gate config). I’ll add that to docs and to the job summary output (prints concurrency + request rate). Pushed in c01b8d0 + doc update in b4b0e52.

Rina Kobayashi (review): For baseline selection, if paired is unavailable we should prefer “last green for same GPU + same model_family + same prompt dist” rather than just same GPU. Otherwise the diff is noisy.

Sahana Iyer (author): Agreed. Implemented baseline key expansion to include model_family + dist id; fallback order is now: paired -> last-green exact key -> last-green same GPU -> non-blocking. See f9d0a11.
Aisha Bello (review): Please add dashboard links that SRE already uses during rollouts so the canary output is consistent with our runbooks. Also avoid linking to per-request traces with raw prompts.

Sahana Iyer (author): Added canonical Grafana dashboard links (selector v2 overview + tail latency by GPU/seq bucket) and removed the trace deep link by default. We only link to trace explorer filtered by run_id and require prompt redaction flag to be enabled. Update in c01b8d0.

Allison Grant (review): On the labels/bucketing: the gate output should use the same bucket names we standardized (short/med/long + prefill/decode) and not raw sequence lengths. Otherwise we risk mismatch with dashboard aggregations.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated schema to emit seq_bucket_name with the standardized enum and keep raw effective_context only in the artifact JSON (not job summary). See 0bb31d1.
Sana Farid (review): Can we make the long-context L4 threshold exception explicit and justified in the config comments? Otherwise people will cargo-cult exceptions.

Sahana Iyer (author): Added a comment block explaining the exception is measurement-variance-driven and temporary, with a TODO to tighten after 2 weeks of baseline collection. Included a link to ENG-3930. (c7c2b8a amended.)
Connor O'Brien (review): I’m fine with merge as long as it’s non-blocking initially. Please confirm the workflow won’t gate runtime release branches until we flip the flag.

Sahana Iyer (author): Confirmed. The workflow posts status but is marked informational only (continue-on-error) for now; we’ll flip to required check via repo settings once baseline week completes. Docs updated in docs/ci/triggering_perf_canary.md.
release_notes: perf-canary: Added selector v2 performance gate (thresholds, baseline selection, and dashboard links) for kernel auto-selection v2 rollout readiness.
